blocks.x: Favorable Health Insurance Rate Allows a Final Reduction

Dr. Mazjanis reported the district's health insurance rate increase came in far better than expected: 3.74%, down from the 10% figure used as recently as the prior week (itself already reduced from an original 15% placeholder). This allows an additional $518,474.37 reduction to the general fund and $13,946.97 across the district's enterprise accounts. Combined with earlier adjustments, this brings the final FY27 budget to $57,349,321.39, a 7.5% increase over FY26 (down from the original 9.88% proposal) and a 7.34% impact on the local tax share.

Dr. Lancia separately flagged a possible future revenue upside unrelated to this budget: a proposed change to the state's EPS education funding formula, moving through the Legislature, would add roughly $125 per low-income-classified student if adopted — an estimated $196,400 for Westbrook, not yet approved and not included in this budget.
Consensus to forward the reduced, 3.74%-insurance-rate budget to the full School Committee for that evening's vote; no roll-call vote recorded.
Request to Reallocate SRO Costs to the City
Chair Mancuso Reports on a Formal Request to City Hall

Chair Mancuso reported she sent a formal written request to City Administrator Angela Holmes, on the School Committee's behalf, asking the City to move the cost-sharing lines for the district's School Resource Officer (SRO) program out of the school budget and into the City's public safety budget. The request emphasized that school leadership highly values the SRO partnership, but argued the program functions primarily as community policing and public safety rather than part of the district's core statutory obligations — notably, one of the largest remaining budget lines not directly tied to education or facilities, at a time when the committee has already cut instructional staff elsewhere.
City Hall has forwarded its municipal budget to City Council, with an expectation the Council will vote on this specific reallocation request after the school budget's own presentation on April 15.
Consensus to formally signal School Committee support for pursuing the reallocation with City Council; no roll-call vote recorded.
